knowledge:
- key_parameters: promWidth=Width of the promoter region around the TSS (e.g., 6000) ;; mode=Method to handle probes mapping to multiple transcripts, such as "union" ;; summarize=Method to summarize reads in promoter regions, typically "add" ;; method=Normalization method for ChIP-seq data, such as "quantile" ;; factor=The phenotype variable of interest in the expression and ChIP-seq data ;; reference=The reference level of the phenotype factor ;; normNull=Indices of the normal components representing the null hypothesis (no change) ;; expNeg=Index of the mirrored exponential component representing negative correlation ;; expPos=Index of the exponential component representing positive correlation ;; itb=Number of burn-in iterations for the Bayesian mixture model ;; nmc=Number of MCMC iterations for the Bayesian mixture model ;; thin=Thinning interval for MCMC sampling
- alternatives: Microarray vs RNA-seq: RNA-seq is preferred because it allows estimating individual transcript abundance and grouping transcripts sharing the same TSS, which simplifies promoter matching. Maximum Likelihood (mlMixModel) vs Bayesian (bayesMixModel): The Bayesian approach is more robust but requires careful tuning of MCMC parameters and convergence diagnostics.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have matched gene transcription data (microarray or RNA-seq) and histone modification ChIP-seq data from the same biological conditions/samples, especially when sample sizes are very small, to identify genes regulated by epigenetic modifications.
- pitfalls: Microarray probes often map to multiple transcripts with different TSSs, requiring careful matching via matchProbeToPromoter. Short MCMC runs (low itb and nmc) in bayesMixModel are unsuitable for real applications; always assess convergence using plotChains. Ensure that the RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data are obtained from the same samples/conditions for meaningful integration.

workflows.name: microarray_chipseq_integration
workflows.intent: Integrate microarray gene expression data with histone ChIP-seq data to classify genes based on concordant or discordant changes.
workflows.stages: 1. Map probes to transcripts and obtain TSS coordinates ;; 2. Calculate promoter regions for each probe using matchProbeToPromoter ;; 3. Summarize ChIP-seq reads in promoter regions using summarizeReads ;; 4. Normalize ChIP-seq data using normalize ;; 5. Integrate expression and ChIP-seq data using integrateData ;; 6. Fit mixture models using mlMixModel or bayesMixModel ;; 7. Plot components and classification using plotComponents and plotClassification
workflows.code:
library(epigenomix)
data(eSet)
pData(eSet)
data(mappedReads)
names(mappedReads)
probeToTrans <- fData(eSet)$transcript
probeToTrans <- strsplit(probeToTrans, ",")
names(probeToTrans) <- featureNames(eSet)
data(transToTSS)
head(transToTSS)
promoters <- matchProbeToPromoter(probeToTrans, transToTSS, promWidth=6000, mode="union")
chipSetRaw <- summarizeReads(mappedReads, promoters, summarize="add")
chipSet <- normalize(chipSetRaw, method="quantile")
chipSet$CEBPA <- factor(c("wt", "ko"))
intData <- integrateData(eSet, chipSet, factor="CEBPA", reference="wt")
head(intData)
mlmm = mlMixModel(intData[,"z"], normNull=c(2, 3), expNeg=1, expPos=4, sdNormNullInit=c(0.5, 1), rateExpNegInit=0.5, rateExpPosInit=0.5, pi=rep(1/4, 4))
mlmm
plotComponents(mlmm, xlim=c(-2, 2), ylim=c(0, 3))
plotClassification(mlmm)
set.seed(1515)
bayesmm = bayesMixModel(intData[,"z"], normNull=c(2, 3), expNeg=1, expPos=4, sdNormNullInit=c(0.5, 1), rateExpNegInit=0.5, rateExpPosInit=0.5, shapeNorm0=c(10, 10), scaleNorm0=c(10, 10), shapeExpNeg0=0.01, scaleExpNeg0=0.01, shapeExpPos0=0.01, scaleExpPos0=0.01, pi=rep(1/4, 4), sdAlpha=1, itb=2000, nmc=8000, thin=5)
bayesmm
plotComponents(bayesmm, xlim=c(-2, 2), ylim=c(0, 3))
plotClassification(bayesmm, method="mode")
table(classification(mlmm, method="maxDens"), classification(bayesmm, method="mode"))
posProbes <- rownames(intData)[classification(bayesmm, method="mode") == 4]

workflows.name: rnaseq_chipseq_integration
workflows.intent: Integrate RNA-seq gene expression data with histone ChIP-seq data to classify genes based on concordant or discordant changes.
input: fpkm (Data frame containing RNA-seq FPKM values and TSS coordinates)
workflows.stages: 1. Construct an ExpressionSet from RNA-seq FPKM data ;; 2. Define promoter regions around TSS coordinates using GRanges and resize ;; 3. Summarize ChIP-seq reads in promoter regions using summarizeReads ;; 4. Normalize ChIP-seq data using normalize ;; 5. Integrate expression and ChIP-seq data using integrateData ;; 6. Fit mixture models using mlMixModel or bayesMixModel
workflows.code:
library(epigenomix)
data(fpkm)
head(fpkm[c(-2,-8), ])
mat <- log2(as.matrix(fpkm[, c("CEBPA_WT", "CEBPA_KO")]))
rownames(mat) <- fpkm$tss_id
eSet.seq <- ExpressionSet(mat)
pData(eSet.seq)$CEBPA <- factor(c("wt", "ko"))
fData(eSet.seq)$chr <- fpkm$chr
fData(eSet.seq)$tss <- fpkm$tss
data(mappedReads)
promoters.seq <- GRanges(seqnames=fData(eSet.seq)$chr, ranges=IRanges(start=fData(eSet.seq)$tss, width=1), probe=featureNames(eSet.seq))
promoters.seq <- resize(promoters.seq, width=3000, fix="center")
promoters.seq <- split(promoters.seq, elementMetadata(promoters.seq)$probe)
chipSetRaw.seq <- summarizeReads(mappedReads, promoters.seq, summarize="add")
chipSetRaw.seq
head(chipVals(chipSetRaw.seq))
chipSet.seq <- normalize(chipSetRaw.seq, method="quantile")
chipSet.seq$CEBPA <- factor(c("wt", "ko"))
intData.seq <- integrateData(eSet.seq, chipSet.seq, factor="CEBPA", reference="wt")
head(intData.seq)
mlmm = mlMixModel(intData.seq[,"z"], normNull=c(2, 3), expNeg=1, expPos=4, sdNormNullInit=c(0.5, 1), rateExpNegInit=0.5, rateExpPosInit=0.5, pi=rep(1/4, 4))
mlmm
